NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the epicenter of the AI infrastructure value chain, designing cutting-edge GPU and networking silicon that is exclusively manufactured by TSMC on advanced nodes and paired with HBM memory from SK Hynix and Micron. Its downstream is dominated by the world's largest hyperscalers and cloud providers—Microsoft, Meta, Google, and Amazon—who are engaged in an unprecedented GPU procurement race to build AI training and inference infrastructure, making NVIDIA both highly powerful and concentrated in its customer exposure.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer that outsources chip fabrication to TSMC and component manufacturing to a global network of suppliers across Asia, while distributing finished products through carriers, retailers, and its own direct channels worldwide. Its downstream relationships are uniquely characterized by a dual role — generating revenue both from end consumers and from platform partners (Google, app developers) who pay significant fees to access Apple's massive installed base of over 2 billion active devices.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain, dependent on a concentrated set of semiconductor equipment makers (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research) for the capital-intensive machinery required to manufacture DRAM and NAND at leading-edge nodes. On the demand side, Micron is heavily exposed to hyperscalers and AI infrastructure builders—particularly NVIDIA for HBM—as well as consumer electronics OEMs, making its revenue highly cyclical and sensitive to cloud capex cycles and smartphone upgrade trends.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP supply chain, designing and licensing CPU/GPU architectures to virtually every major chip company rather than manufacturing silicon itself. Its upstream dependencies are primarily EDA software vendors and cloud infrastructure providers, while its downstream customer base spans mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT semiconductor markets — making ARM's revenue highly correlated with global chip design activity and silicon unit shipment volumes.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company that sits at a critical juncture in the data infrastructure supply chain, relying heavily on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing while serving hyperscale cloud providers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and networking OEMs with custom ASICs, Ethernet silicon, and storage controllers. Its strategic pivot toward AI-driven custom silicon (XPUs) for cloud data centers has significantly elevated its dependency on leading-edge foundry capacity and deepened its revenue concentration among a handful of major hyperscaler customers.
